lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach succulent leaf architecture plus a starry flower with multiple separate carpels and follicular fruit as the Crassulaceae branch of Saxifragales.

project_scope.note: The current pool contains Sedum nuttallii plus the historical synonym row Sedum nuttallianum. Current Kew accepts S. nuttallii and synonymizes S. nuttallianum.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with succulent leaves, then inspect the flower center. Crassulaceae commonly has a star-like 4–5-merous flower, stamens equal to or twice the petal number, and several separate or basally joined carpels that mature into follicles.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly succulent herbs or subshrubs; leaves simple, fleshy, alternate/opposite/whorled, stipules absent.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers commonly bisexual and radial; sepals and petals usually 4–5; stamens often twice as many as petals; small nectar scales sit at the base of each carpel.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A cluster of follicles, usually one follicle per carpel, containing few to many seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Succulent herb + starry flower + several distinct carpels/follicles is the stonecrop-family package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: succulent leaf → star flower → stamen count → separate carpels → follicles → synonym card
visual_lesson.intro: Crassulaceae becomes easy once you stop at the flower center: the carpels stay visibly separate and later become a ring of follicles.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the succulent leaves
steps.look_for: Small fleshy water-storing leaves on a low herb.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fast gestalt, though succulence alone is not enough.

steps.title: 2 · Count petals and stamens
steps.look_for: Star-shaped flower, commonly 5 petals with about 10 stamens in Sedum.
steps.why_it_matters: The doubled stamen count is a useful stonecrop pattern.

steps.title: 3 · Find the separate carpels
steps.look_for: Several carpels arranged in a ring, each with its own style, rather than one fully fused ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a powerful family confirmation character.

steps.title: 4 · Follow each carpel into a follicle
steps.look_for: A cluster of dry follicles opening along one side.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit preserves the multi-carpel architecture seen in the flower.

steps.title: 5 · Collapse the duplicate source name
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents one native stonecrop from appearing twice in the learner.

comparisons.title: Crassulaceae vs Cactaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are succulent, but Crassulaceae usually retains ordinary fleshy leaves and starry flowers with several carpels/follicles; cacti use areoles and a very different stem/flower architecture.

comparisons.title: Crassulaceae vs Saxifragaceae-like plants
comparisons.rule: Stonecrops are strongly succulent and commonly have several follicles; saxifrages are usually not strongly succulent and often have fewer, more fused carpels.

visual_lesson.caveat: Succulence evolved repeatedly. Always confirm the flower center and fruit rather than calling every succulent Crassulaceae.

genera.fast_cue: small succulent herb + starry flower + multiple carpels/follicles

visual_targets.annotation_goal: connect each follicle back to a carpel
